parsed.explanation: No trans-specific offence: the cross-dressing law was struck down by the final court of appeal in 2018, and no facility, custody, border or care restriction is documented — so no universal-exposure tier-1 rule is evidenced, and the absent LGR regime is a resident-only gap. Against this, documented police use of residual summary clauses to extort LGBT people (a known lever on visibly gender-nonconforming people) and a justice failure where a stabbed trans woman was barred from court and her case dismissed (2017, dated) plus a 69-case violence tally with no denominator and no hate-crime recourse push it down. Countervailing: 72% acceptance in 2022, pride parades under police protection, official retraining cooperation, and cross-party backing for decriminalisation. The sodomy statute is an unenforced secondary lever, not dominant. Repeated visitor-facing harms with incomplete remedy and open questions place this in the elevated-to-reduced boundary, below the acceptance-with-protections tier.
